clue.text: Arrive at a state of consciousness

definitions.text: Arrive at a state of consciousness

parts.words: Arrive at a state of consciousness
parts.note: the phrase for reaching a total also means waking after a faint, so the whole clue describes regaining awareness

explanation.surface: Someone surfaces into awareness.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover after fainting is to reach consciousness again, the idiom for reviving.

clue.text: Make things even worse for the pound

explanation.surface: Something makes matters worse for sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound sign is drawn as a capital letter L, so the phrase split differently names the symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to crown a run of bad luck; read as two words plus a letter it describes the sterling symbol.

clue.text: Invented a story and settled the argument

explanation.surface: Someone fabricated a tale and ended a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fabricated a tale, and also reconciled after a quarrel.

clue.text: Work until I left

parts.note: to means until, as in nine to five

explanation.surface: Someone keeps working until they alone have departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour and hard graft are synonyms for the word.

clue.text: Eccentrics dancing every other night?

explanation.surface: Odd people go dancing on alternate evenings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the second part is dances held on odd-numbered nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar people are oddballs; dances on odd nights would be odd balls.

clue.text: Contends diet changes result in feeling unsatisfied

indicators.note: changes tells the solver the letters of the two words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone argues that altering their diet leaves them dissatisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unhappy with one's lot is a synonym for discontent.

clue.text: Disheartened sahib upset by prejudice

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the remaining letters are turned upside down, read from bottom to top
the heart of the word is its central letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: A colonial gentleman is upset by bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes the middle H of SAHIB, leaving SAIB; 'upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a one-sided leaning, a synonym of partiality.

clue.text: A teaching derived from a Bible reading

explanation.surface: A moral drawn from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is an instructive teaching, and also the passage of scripture read aloud in a church service.

clue.text: Very old diocese that encompasseth nought

indicators.note: an archaic form of encompasses, meaning the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a see is the area under a bishop, a diocese
nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: An ancient diocese with nothing in it, in mock-biblical language.
explanation.definitionFit: Being senile means being frail with advanced age, a near synonym.

clue.text: Native language requiring one Director General to enter credit card code

indicators.note: to enter means the letters go inside another piece

parts.note: PIN is the personal identification number for a card
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A local tongue somehow requires a senior official to type in a card number.
explanation.definitionFit: A pidgin is a simplified contact language that arises among native speakers of different tongues.

clue.text: Two fools take in a murderous type

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and two of them are needed
the second ass of the pair
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of idiots harbour a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer, often of a public figure.

clue.text: Two articles recommend poetry from opposite ends of the earth

parts.note: the is the definite article
an is the indefinite article
to tip is to recommend, as a tip for a race
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Grammar words and verse are recommended from far-flung places.
explanation.definitionFit: The term for places diametrically opposite on the globe, used in Britain for Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Neat haircut

explanation.surface: A tidy cut at the barber's.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means tidy; as a noun a light cut of the hair.

clue.text: Cry for work to be given to UN health agency

indicators.note: to be given to means the work piece is attached after the agency

parts.note: WHO is the World Health Organization, part of the United Nations
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A demand that a task be handed to the World Health Organization.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud shout of joy or excitement.

clue.text: To treat it prepare water for a poultice

definitions.text: To treat it prepare water for a poultice

parts.words: To treat it prepare water for a poultice
parts.note: a skin abscess is traditionally treated with a hot poultice, which needs water heated; the word for heating water also names the abscess

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a hot dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boil is a painful pus-filled swelling, and boiling is heating water, so one word does both jobs.

clue.text: The Wilde award for acting

explanation.surface: A prize for performance named after a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar was Wilde's first name, and the Oscar is the Academy Award statuette given for film acting.

clue.text: Fine the school menace

explanation.surface: A penalty imposed on the playground tormentor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bully is old slang for excellent, as in bully for you, and also a pupil who intimidates others.

clue.text: His work in chemistry represented a sole pursuit

indicators.note: represented means the letters are presented anew, rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A scientist's chemical research described as a single-minded pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nods at the man: his chemistry was indeed a single-minded pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French chemist and microbiologist known for pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: Leaving-apparently with a bang!

explanation.surface: Someone departs noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means departing, and also exploding like a bomb or firework.

clue.text: Cut off East Anglian city without compunction

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, in eastern England

explanation.surface: A city in eastern England is isolated without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting harshly and without mercy is acting sternly, the adverb's sense here.

clue.text: Dissipated character of an erratic seam bowler

definitions.text: character of an erratic seam bowler

explanation.surface: A cricketer's wayward bowling style is morally lax.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a seam bowler delivers the ball at speed; one who is erratic could be called quick and wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing fast and loose means behaving recklessly and irresponsibly; an erratic quick bowler is literally fast and loose.

clue.text: One who exhibits a spray

explanation.surface: An exhibitor of a spray.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who displays things is a show-er; a shower is also a fine spray of water.

clue.text: Nervous Pole took it to heart

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
cared means felt concern, took something to heart

explanation.surface: A Polish person was upset by something.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened and anxious are synonyms.

clue.text: Pop or white wine

explanation.surface: Fizzy drink or a glass of white.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop is slang for to pawn, as is to hock; hock is also German white wine from the Rhine.

clue.text: Maybe top people cause distress

explanation.surface: The elite may be upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a set of people who are up, the elite; as one word it means to distress.

clue.text: Formerly 1/100

parts.note: one with a hundred placed in it: the figure 1 spelt out, with C, the Roman hundred, put inside

explanation.surface: A bare fraction, once worth a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the slash as one wrapped round a hundred: the word one, with C (the Roman hundred) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at one time in the past.

clue.text: In France I hesitate to boo

parts.note: je is French for I
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A French speaker hesitates before booing.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock with shouts, a synonym of boo.

clue.text: "Hall to thee, blithe Spirit! Bird thou never "(Tea Skylark)

definitions.text: "Hall to thee, blithe Spirit! Bird thou never "(Tea Skylark)

parts.words: "Hall to thee, blithe Spirit! Bird thou never "(Tea Skylark)
parts.note: the opening line of Shelley's ode To a Skylark, with its last word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A famous line of Romantic poetry with its final word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's OCR prints 'Hall' for Hail and 'Tea' for To a; the poem is Shelley's To a Skylark.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic past tense of be with thou supplies the missing word in Shelley's verse.

clue.text: Military chiefs carried on ICBMs

explanation.surface: Generals ride on intercontinental missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: War heads would be army leaders; warheads are the explosive tips of missiles.

clue.text: If you can't borrow one or steal one, vamoose!

definitions.text: If you can't borrow one or steal one

explanation.surface: Advice to someone short of something: get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it is the last resort after borrowing or stealing; as one it is an order to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command to leave at once, like the slang vamoose.

clue.text: It provides relief when embarrassed and angry

parts.note: people go red when embarrassed
cross means angry

explanation.surface: Something soothes when you are both ashamed and annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The international humanitarian organisation brings aid to disaster victims.

clue.text: Close to being strait laced

explanation.surface: Almost being prim.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffy means airless, like close weather, and also prim and old-fashioned.
